arxiv-2103-16819.title: Comparing the Inner and Outer Star Forming Complexes in the Nearby Spiral Galaxies NGC 628, NGC 5457 and NGC 6946 using UVIT Observations Facilities: Astrosat(UVIT), GALEX, VLA Source Extractor ( Bertin & Arnouts 1996 ; Barbary 2016 ) , topcat ( Taylor 2005 ) , IRAF ( Tody 1993 ) , Astropy ( Astropy
arxiv-2103-16819.creator: Jyoti Yadav, Mousumi Das, Narendra Nath Patra, K. S. Dwarakanath, P. T. Rahna, Stacy S. McGaugh, James Schombert, Jayant Murthy
arxiv-2103-16819.description: Abstract We present a far-UV (FUV) study of the star-forming complexes (SFCs) in three nearby galaxies using the Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (UVIT). The galaxies are close to face-on and show significant outer disk star formation. Two of them are isolated (NGC 628, NGC 6946), and one is interacting with distant companions (NGC 5457).

arxiv-2203-05694.title: Internal mode-induced growth in 3 3 d nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations Thanks: F.P. was supported in part by a start-up grant from the University of Toronto, and NSERC grant RGPIN-2018-06487.
arxiv-2203-05694.creator: Tristan Léger, Fabio Pusateri
arxiv-2203-05694.description: Abstract . This note complements the paper [ 20 ] by proving a scattering statement for solutions of nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations with an internal mode in 3 3 d. We show that small solutions exhibit growth around a one-dimensional set in frequency space and become of order one in L ∞ L^{\infty} after a short transient time.

arxiv-2211-10187.title: Void Lensing in Cubic Galileon Gravity
arxiv-2211-10187.creator: Chen Su, Huanyuan Shan, Jiajun Zhang, Cheng Zhao, Jiaxi Yu, Qiao Wang, Linfeng Xiao, Xiangkun Liu, An Zhao
arxiv-2211-10187.description: Abstract Weak lensing studies via cosmic voids are a promising probe of Modified Gravity (MG). Excess surface mass density (ESD) is widely used as a lensing statistic in weak lensing research. In this paper, we use the ray-tracing method to study the ESD around voids in simulations based on Cubic Galileon (CG) gravity.

arxiv-2401-04200.title: Teacher bias or measurement error?
arxiv-2401-04200.creator: Thomas van Huizen, Madelon Jacobs, Matthijs Oosterveen
arxiv-2401-04200.description: Abstract In many countries, teachers’ track recommendations are used to allocate students to secondary school tracks. Previous studies have shown that students from families with low socioeconomic status (SES) receive lower track recommendations than their peers from high SES families, conditional on standardized test scores. It is often argued that this indicates teacher bias.

arxiv-2401-09269.title: Direct N N -body simulations of satellite formation around small asteroids: insights from DART’s encounter with the Didymos system Journal: PSJ pkdgrav ( Richardson et al. 2000 ; Schwartz et al. 2012 ; Zhang et al. 2017 ) , REBOUND ( Rein & Liu 2012 ) , REBOUNDx ( Tamayo et al. 2020 ) , Persistence
arxiv-2401-09269.creator: Harrison F. Agrusa, Yun Zhang, Derek C. Richardson, Petr Pravec, Matija Ćuk, Patrick Michel, Ronald-Louis Ballouz, Seth A. Jacobson, Daniel J. Scheeres, Kevin Walsh, Olivier Barnouin, R. Terik Daly, Eric Palmer, Maurizio Pajola, Alice Lucchetti, Filippo Tusberti, Joseph V. DeMartini, Fabio Ferrari,
arxiv-2401-09269.description: Abstract We explore binary asteroid formation by spin-up and rotational disruption considering the NASA DART mission’s encounter with the Didymos-Dimorphos binary, which was the first small binary visited by a spacecraft. Using a suite of N N -body simulations, we follow the gravitational accumulation of a satellite from meter-sized particles following a mass-shedding event from a rapidly rotating primary.

arxiv-2407-12414.title: Extremal fixed points and Diophantine equations
arxiv-2407-12414.creator: Christopher P. Herzog a , Christian B. Jepsen b , Hugh Osborn c and Yaron Oz d
arxiv-2407-12414.description: Abstract The coupling constants of fixed points in the ϵ \epsilon expansion at one loop are known to satisfy a quadratic bound due to Rychkov and Stergiou. We refer to fixed points that saturate this bound as extremal fixed points .

arxiv-2412-04873.title: Bullet pressure-cell design for neutron scattering experiments with horizontal magnetic fields and dilution temperatures
arxiv-2412-04873.creator: Ellen Fogh ∗, Gaétan Giriat, Richard Gaal, Oleksandr Prokhnenko, Maciej Bartkowiak, Luc Testa, Jana Pásztorová, Ekaterina Pomjakushina, Yoshiya Uwatoko, Hiroyuki Nojiri, Koji Munakata, Kazuhisa Kakurai, Henrik M. Rønnow
arxiv-2412-04873.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ellen Fogh ∗, Gaétan Giriat, Richard Gaal, Oleksandr Prokhnenko, Maciej Bartkowiak, Luc Testa, Jana Pásztorová, Ekaterina Pomjakushina, Yoshiya Uwatoko, Hiroyuki Nojiri, Koji Munakata, Kazuhisa Kakurai, Henrik M. Rønnow. The simultaneous application of high magnetic fields and high pressures for controlling magnetic ground states is important for testing our understanding of many-body quantum theory. However, the implementation for neutron scattering experiments presents a technical challenge.

arxiv-2503-01697.title: Krylov shadow tomography: Efficient estimation of quantum Fisher information
arxiv-2503-01697.creator: Da-Jian Zhang, D. M. Tong
arxiv-2503-01697.description: Abstract Efficiently estimating the quantum Fisher information (QFI) is pivotal in quantum information science but remains an outstanding challenge for large systems due to its high nonlinearity. In this Letter, we tackle this long-standing challenge by integrating the Krylov subspace method–a celebrated tool from applied mathematics–into the framework of shadow tomography.

arxiv-2506-13484.title: Deep Diffusion Models and Unsupervised Hyperspectral Unmixing for Realistic Abundance Map Synthesis
arxiv-2506-13484.creator: Martina Pastorino, Michael Alibani, Nicola Acito, Gabriele Moser
arxiv-2506-13484.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel methodology for generating realistic abundance maps from hyperspectral imagery using an unsupervised, deep-learning-driven approach. Our framework integrates blind linear hyperspectral unmixing with state-of-the-art diffusion models to enhance the realism and diversity of synthetic abundance maps. First, we apply blind unmixing to extract endmembers and abundance maps directly from raw hyperspectral data.

arxiv-2508-05654.title: COMPARISON OF INFORMATION RETRIEVAL TECHNIQUES APPLIED TO IT SUPPORT TICKETS
arxiv-2508-05654.creator: Leonardo Santiago Benitez Pereira, Robinson Pizzio, and Samir Bonho
arxiv-2508-05654.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Leonardo Santiago Benitez Pereira, Robinson Pizzio, and Samir Bonho. Institutions dependent on IT services and resources acknowledge the crucial significance of an IT help desk system, that act as a centralized hub connecting IT staff and users for service requests. Employing various Machine Learning models, these IT help desk systems allow access to corrective actions used in the past, but each model has different performance when applied to different datasets.

arxiv-2510-06696.title: Provability Models
arxiv-2510-06696.creator: Mojtaba Mojtahedi, Borja Sierra Miranda
arxiv-2510-06696.description: Abstract In this paper, we study a new Kripke-style semantics for classical modal logic, named as provability models. We study provability models for the propositional modal logics 𝖪 {\sf K} , 𝖪𝟦 {\sf K4} , 𝖲𝟦 {\sf S4} 𝖦𝖫 {\sf GL} , 𝖦𝖫𝖯 {\sf GLP} and the interpretability logic 𝖨𝖫𝖬 {\sf ILM} .

arxiv-2601-08642.title: Cities at Play: Improving Equilibria in Urban Neighbourhood Games
arxiv-2601-08642.creator: Martin Gairing, Adrian Vetta, Zhanzhan Zhao
arxiv-2601-08642.description: Abstract How should cities invest to improve social welfare when individuals respond strategically to local conditions? We model this question using a game-theoretic version of Schelling’s bounded neighbourhood model, where agents choose neighbourhoods based on concave, non-monotonic utility functions reflecting local population.

britannica-1911-mortain.title: Mortain (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-mortain.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-mortain.description: Article 'Mortain' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. France, the chief town of an arrondissement and seat of a sub-prefect. It is beautifully situated on a rocky hill rising above the gorge of the Cance, a tributary of the Sélune. The parish church of St Évroult is a magnificent example of the transitional style of the early 13th century, with a massive tower of the 14th and a Norman doorway dating from the original collegiate church (1058).

pmc-10568275.title: Application of sample size re-estimation in clinical trials: A systematic review
pmc-10568275.creator: Hirotaka Mano, Yuji Tanaka, Shunichiro Orihara, Junji Moriya
pmc-10568275.description: BackgroundSample size re-estimation (SSR) is a method used to recalculate sample size during clinical trial conduct to address a lack of adequate information and can have a significant impact on study size, duration, resources, and cost. Few studies to date have summarized the conditions and circumstances under which SSR is applied.

pmc-11478618.title: Exploring the Potential of Pectin as a Source of Biopolymers for Active and Intelligent Packaging: A Review
pmc-11478618.creator: Andi Dirpan, Yosini Deliana, Andi Fadiah Ainani, Irwan, Nur Alim Bahmid
pmc-11478618.description: The use of fossil-based plastics in food packaging poses a serious environmental concern. Pectin, a natural biodegradable polymer, offers a potential solution for environmentally friendly and sustainable food packaging to replace fossil-based plastics. This article reviews the applications of pectin in active and intelligent packaging and analyzes the latest research trends.

pmc-12431287.title: EMBRAVE: EMBedded Remote Attestation and Verification framEwork
pmc-12431287.creator: Enrico Bravi, Alessio Claudio, Antonio Lioy, Andrea Vesco, Jinbo Xiong
pmc-12431287.description: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a growing area of interest with an increasing number of applications, including cyber–physical systems (CPS). Emerging threats in the IoT context make software integrity verification a key solution for checking that IoT platforms have not been tampered with so that they behave as expected.

pmc-12471135.title: An Expendable Player in Positive Vascular Remodeling? ADAMTS13 Deficiency Does Not Affect Arteriogenesis or Angiogenesis
pmc-12471135.creator: Carolin Baur, Amanda Geml, Kira-Sofie Wimmer, Franziska Heim, Anja Holschbach, Katharina Elbs, Michael R. Rohrmoser, Dominic van den Heuvel, Alexander T. Bauer, Stefan W. Schneider, Daphne Merkus, Elisabeth Deindl
pmc-12471135.description: Peripheral artery disease is a common manifestation of atherosclerosis, characterized by insufficient tissue perfusion and chronic ischemia. Arteriogenesis and angiogenesis are essential endogenous mechanisms to restore blood flow and limit ischemic injury. The metalloprotease ADAMTS13, known for cleaving ultra-large von Willebrand factor, has been implicated in thrombotic and inflammatory regulation. However, its role in ischemic vascular remodeling remains unclear.

pmc-12963108.title: Immediate and delayed effects of thermal stress on fever-associated seizures in children: A time-stratified case-crossover study in Japan
pmc-12963108.creator: Naomi Matsumoto, Yuka Yamamura, Kensuke Uraguchi, Takafumi Obara, Hiromichi Naito, Takashi Yorifuji
pmc-12963108.description: This study aimed to examine the non-linear and delayed effects of thermal stress, measured by the hourly Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI), on the risk of pediatric fever-associated seizures (FAS). We conducted a time-stratified case-crossover study in Okayama, Japan (May 2015–March 2023), analyzing 3,201 ambulance-attended FAS cases in children younger than 7 years.

pmc-13183709.title: Evidence of the role of Midkine and Pleiotrophin in the pathogenesis of Familial Mediterranean Fever
pmc-13183709.creator: Zeinab Y Abdallah, Ghada Nour Eldeen, Mona F Sokkar, Rania Fawzy Mahmoud abdelkawy, Randa S Lotfy, Shymaa H Hussein, Khaled Hamed, Hala T El-Bassyouni
pmc-13183709.description: Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) is a chronic autoinflammatory illness that follows a pattern of periodic attacks; however, the majority of cases experience ongoing subclinical inflammation during the attack-free periods that could lead to the development of anemia, splenomegaly, heart disease, and the major complication, amyloidosis. Midkine/Pleiotrophin (MDK/PTN) are heparin-binding cytokines, with upregulated expression in various inflammatory and malignant diseases.

pmc-13462084.title: Conserved macromolecular architecture of poplar secondary cell walls revealed by ssNMR and atomistic modeling
pmc-13462084.creator: Bennett Addison, Malitha C. Dickwella Widanage, Meagan F. Crowley, Vivek S. Bharadwaj, Lintao Bu, Michael F. Crowley, Anne E. Harman-Ware, Peter N. Ciesielski
pmc-13462084.description: The macromolecular architecture of plant secondary cell walls governs wood’s mechanical and biochemical properties, yet its natural intra-species variability remains poorly characterized. Here, we combined ¹³C solid-state NMR (ssNMR), multivariate statistical analysis, and molecular modeling to profile nanoscale structure across 13 genetically diverse Populus trichocarpa genotypes grown in ¹³C-enriched atmospheres.

pmc-13463616.title: Apical proximal tubule fatty acid uptake–generated ceramides cause endoplasmic reticulum stress from altered membrane fluidity
pmc-13463616.creator: Zhiyu Liu, Robert J Gaivin, Shenaz Khan, Vincent Li, Amal Chaba, Fraser J Moss, Usman Sabir, Takhar Kasumov, Tingwei Mu, Jeffrey R Schelling

pmc-13518217.title: Biosynthesis and enzymology of azaindane natural products
pmc-13518217.creator: Zhiyang Quan, Takayoshi Awakawa
pmc-13518217.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). As a representative example of biosynthetic genome mining aimed at identifying biosynthetic gene clusters whose target is unknown core enzymes for known natural products, we review the biosynthesis of altemicidin (1), SB-203207 (2), and SB-203208 (3). Self-resistance gene-guided genome mining led to the identification of the responsible biosynthetic gene cluster, and heterologous expression of the cluster successfully confirmed the production of compounds 1–3.
